title: Not Cross-Charging Head Office Costs Does Not by Itself Prove GST Evasion, Rules Gujarat High Court in Amul's Favour
case_name: Gujarat Co-operative Milk Marketing Federation Limited (Amul) v. Union of India & Ors.
citation: Division Bench of Justices A.S. Supehia and Vaibhavi D. Nanavati; neutral citation not stated in sources reviewed
card_summary: The Gujarat High Court set aside a Rs 43.43 crore IGST demand against Amul, holding that a head office's failure to cross-charge common expenses to branches for 2017-19 does not alone prove fraud or suppression under Section 74 of the CGST Act. The authorities had shown no grounds for that extended limitation, and the court valued the inter-unit services at nil under Rule 28, since no invoices passed between units.
card_tip: A department invoking Section 74's extended limitation for an inter-unit cross-charging lapse must show fraud or wilful suppression, not merely a failure to cross-charge, or the demand is open to challenge.
verification_notes: Decision outcome, bench, demand amount and reasoning are consistent across Taxscan, LiveLawBiz, A2Z Taxcorp and Dairy News Today. Sources differ on whether the judgment was delivered on 14, 15 or 16 October 2026; one report's reference to a 'Wednesday' hearing points to 14 October 2026, which is used here, but the exact date could not be independently confirmed from the order itself. No case number or neutral citation was available in the sources reviewed.
